Liberia and India represent two indispensable pillars of the international maritime architecture. Together, we are the picture of what goes across our waters every day and night. The Group of Friends unites our nations around three non-negotiable imperatives. First and foremost is safety, demanding uncompromising technical standards, stringent vessel compliance, and coordinating environmental stewardship to prevent loss of life and marine degradation. Secondly, security of shipping itself, defending commercial sea lanes against piracy, armed attacks, regional instability, and asymmetric threats that are changing every day. Thirdly, seafarers. Centering the human beings who keep our world running. Seafarers must never be treated as expendable cargo that can just be dumped over the docks, over the sea, and thrown into unforgetfulness. We are joining hands to address crew abandonment, uphold fair labor standards, ensure rapid medical assistance, and protect crews transiting conflict corridors. Let me emphasize that the Group of Friends is not a symbolic gesture. It's an action-driven, multilateral coalition within the framework of the International Maritime Organization and the International Labor Organization.
